newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen-Hard for Germany to hit EMU fiscal goals.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen-Hard for Germany to hit EMU fiscal goals.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Thursday that it would be tough for Germany to fulfil the fiscal criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start in January 1999.
"It is becoming increasingly evident, that Germany will find it extraordinarily difficult to meet the budget and debt criteria," Jochimsen told Germany's monthly magazine Die Neue Gesellschaft.
Countries face strict entry criteria to join currency union, including low budget deficits, government debt and stable exchange rates.
Jochimsen also said that any delay in the planned January 1, 1999 start date laid down in the Maastricht Treaty could not be categorically ruled out.
The question of delay should not be made taboo, or made into a question of "war and peace" the magazine reported Jochimsen as saying in an interview.
But Jochimsen added that any delay in the timetable should be to a precisely-defined later date.
Jochimsen added that a hasty start to monetary union with unprepared nations included was possible, but could not last.
